summary.intent: Plan and then execute GSD Phase 69 for CipherBox — porting the node/v3 model (Node/SealedChildRef/PublishedNode, AAD-sealed crypto, resumable rotation engine) into the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack, making clients grant-root-aware, mirroring the TS Phase 68.2 SDK-owned read chain.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (18 plans across waves) and 13/18 plans merged green (full crates/core + crates/sdk node/v3 foundation: codec/seal, gated read-chain, resumable rotation engine, write-plane emit API, write-owner materialization API). The FUSE consumer cutover (69-09) proved to be an atomic >1000-site, ~12k LOC crypto-model rewrite with no compiling sub-unit; after three successive architectural blockers and re-scopes, the user approved a bounded multi-session 'slice' grind (S1-S5) gated on a live sdk-e2e/desktop-e2e run rather than compile-green, and slices 1-3 (InodeKind reshape, read materialization, write emission) landed with the crate still expectedly RED pending slices 4-5.

repo: CipherBox Rust workspace splits node/v3 across crates/core (pure Node enum/codec/seal), crates/sdk (stateful listing/rotation/emit), crates/fuse (FUSE/WinFsp adapter), crates/api-client, crates/crypto.
D-04 mandates a clean flag-day cutover (no dual-model bridge) since there are no production vaults yet — greenfield migration is preferred over backwards-compat shims.

D-07 requires dual-keying: SealedChildRef (read plane, keyed by ipnsName) vs WriteChildRef (write plane, keyed by childId UUID) — pairing must be by node identity (published.id == WriteChildRef.child_id), never by ipnsName.

Terminal-owner zeroization rule: only zero self-minted keys, never caller-owned/borrowed buffers; enforced by passing parent_read_key/parent_write_key as borrows (&[u8]) so the type system prevents zeroing them.

crates/fuse/Cargo.toml gates Windows/WinFsp code behind default=['fuse'] and #[cfg(feature='winfsp')] — excluded from default `cargo check --workspace`, only verified under `--features winfsp` in the cargo-windows CI lane.
68.2 TS reference branch must be read via `git show <ref>:<path>`, never `git checkout`, when it's already checked out elsewhere in the same repo.

InodeKind (crates/fuse/src/inode.rs) is a read-WRITE vault-owner structure (holds ipns_private_key to sign IPNS records, plus folder_key/file_key) — not a read-only client like the web 68.2 mirror, so read-only listing APIs (ResolvedChild) can't feed it directly.

crates/sdk/src/queue.rs JournalOp had only hex-string ECIES-under-user-key fields (wrapped_key_hex, parent_ipns_key_hex, etc.) — the original research's cited 'parent_metadata: FolderMetadata' cross-crate weld didn't actually exist there (it was in fuse's local MkdirJournalResult).

ApiNodeFetcher<'a> is a lifetime-bound borrow adapter with no `::new` constructor — must be constructed inline at each call site (e.g. `ApiNodeFetcher { api: self.api.as_ref() }`), not stored as a struct field (would be self-referential).
NodeContent.file_iv is hex-encoded (matches legacy iv_hex decode path in content_ops.rs) — a convention future write-path code must match.
Only 3 real CipherBoxFS{..} struct-literal construction sites exist (test_support.rs, desktop mod.rs, desktop windows/mod.rs); other files referencing CipherBoxFS are impl blocks, not constructions.

WriteQueue.journal_dir is pub(crate) and unreachable from crates/fuse — RotationHighWater must be derived from the local journal_dir captured before it moves into WriteQueue::new, not read back from the queue.

code.finding: ResolvedChild carries no key material ({ipns_name, name, kind, size, modified_at, sequence}); resolve_child unseals then immediately zeroizes the child read-key and never touches the write-body — insufficient for a read-write FUSE owner.

JournalOp::{UploadFile,MkdirPublish} reshaped in 69-18 to carry child_published_node (base64 PublishedNode), parent_child_ref (SealedChildRef), parent_write_child_ref (WriteChildRef) instead of legacy hex-ECIES fields.

InodeKind reshaped (69-09 Slice 1) to Root/Folder/File variants each carrying non-Option read_key/write_key/ipns_private_key (Zeroizing types), dropping legacy encrypted_folder_key/folder_key/file_meta_ipns_name/versions fields.
build_child_refs pre-existing clippy too-many-args warning noted as not-mine during 69-17 review.

workflow: GSD's commit helper reports a false-negative 'commit_failed' even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

Worktree-isolated executor agents sometimes mis-report `expected_base` as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork base — verify the real fork point via `git merge-base worktree-agent-<id> HEAD` before recording/merging.
cargo fmt run at the crate root can over-reformat unrelated files beyond an agent's intended scope — executors should scope-check and revert unrelated fmt drift before committing.

When a background worktree executor dies mid-stream (API stall) with uncommitted-but-substantially-complete work, it's often faster to finish the last small pending edit directly in its worktree and commit (with --no-verify if the worktree lacks node_modules for husky) than to fully re-dispatch.
When an executor's SUMMARY.md is missing because it died before writing one, the orchestrator can backfill a SUMMARY by matching a sibling plan's format so tracking stays honest.

For an atomic all-or-nothing crypto-model migration (RED mid-flip by design), gate the final merge on cargo-green PLUS a live e2e test run, not compile-green alone — compile-clean crypto has shipped runtime-broken before (48/89 E2E broke on a zeroization bug; D-07 conflation shipped compile-clean).

When a large atomic plan can't be executed in one autonomous pass, decompose it into a runbook of bounded 'slices' with a frozen authoritative target shape (e.g., InodeKind field set) committed to disk, so each slice-executor works against a stable contract and progress survives usage-limit interruptions.

A 'stop and report rather than force broken/unverifiable work to look complete' norm was followed repeatedly by executors — genuine architectural blockers were halted with zero edits made, preserving the green baseline, rather than grinding out an unverifiable partial migration.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run (API error) after writing 13/14 plans, requiring filesystem-fallback recovery and a fresh single-plan planner dispatch for the missing plan.
Two background executor agents died mid-task from API errors/session limits (stream stall, and 'hit session limit resets 2pm'), losing partial in-progress work or requiring resumption.

Three successive in-execution architectural discoveries on the FUSE cutover (69-09): first that read/write migration were coupled beyond the plan's scope, then that write-plane emit infra didn't exist at all, then that a write-owner tree-materialization API and JournalOp wire-format were also missing — each requiring a new research+plan+approval cycle.

The atomic 69-09 flip turned out to span >1000 sites (~12,300 LOC) across InodeKind, populate_folder, content_ops, write_ops, replay.rs, and desktop glue, with no compiling sub-unit until the very end — making a single-executor pass infeasible and requiring manual slice decomposition.

Local worktree environment lacked node_modules, causing husky pre-commit hooks to fail on first commit attempts in fresh worktrees (worked around via pnpm install or --no-verify for pure-Rust changes).
cwd drifted mid-session causing a runbook write to go to a doubled/incorrect scratchpad path, requiring a manual move to the correct location.
open_items: Complete the remaining 69-09 grind slices: S4 (replay.rs re-publish + fail-closed skip) and S5 (glue + desktop sites + SC#6 CI gate + a new gated file-node fetch wrapper, e.g. fetch_node_gated) to reach cargo-green.
After cargo-green, run a real local sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e (docker + TEE) verification pass before merging the combined 69-18+69-09 branch — this is the agreed merge gate, not compile-green alone.
Verify file `versions` (VersionEntry) restoration at E2E since InodeKind dropped the versions field in Slice 1 and it's not yet reconstructed at upload — flagged as a possible regression to check.
After 69-09 merges: execute 69-10 (delete legacy crates/core types) and 69-13 (grant-gated write + SC#2 + D-07 CI gate).
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows + TEST-03, autonomous:false) is intentionally deferred/handed off — requires the user's Windows machine.
The `phase uat-passed` GSD CLI gap and phase-complete false-warning issues (from prior memory) remain unaddressed workarounds, not touched in this session.
